Feature: GPIO Register Reset Defaults and Masked Read/Write
Test Description: Verify reset default values and masked read/write behavior of per-pin GPIO registers (GPIO_8 through GPIO_27). Confirm that only writable fields change on write and non-writable fields retain their default values; read comparisons are performed only on readable fields.
Meta Test Description: The test iterates over a defined list of per-pin GPIO registers (GPIO_8..GPIO_27). For each register entry: (1) Reset/default verification: If the register is marked readable and not skipped for reset check, read the register, apply the documented read mask, and compare the masked value with the documented default value. (2) Masked write/read verification: For each test data value, if the register is writable (per write mask), write the data masked by the write mask. If the register is also readable (per read mask), read back, apply the read mask, and verify against an expected value composed of writable-field bits from the written data and non-writable-field bits preserved from the default value. Any mismatch increments a failure counter. The test reports PASS only if no default or write/read mismatches are recorded.
Remarks: Non-writable fields in each GPIO register must retain their default values after writes. Read and write operations should be validated only on fields permitted by the respective masks for each GPIO register.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) For each GPIO register from GPIO_8 to GPIO_27, read the register where readable and compare the masked value to the documented reset default. 2) For each GPIO register that is writable, write a set of representative data values masked by its write mask. 3) For each such write, read back the register where readable and compare the masked read value against the expected value formed by writable bits from the written data and default-preserved bits for non-writable fields. 4) Record any mismatches observed during default or masked write/read checks. 5) Declare PASS if no mismatches are recorded across all registers; otherwise declare FAIL.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure: Initialization: Initialize counters for default-check failures and write/read failures. Define the list of target GPIO registers and per-register attributes (address, default value, read mask, write mask, skip flags). Default check: For each GPIO entry, if reset-check is not skipped and the read mask is nonzero, read the register value, apply the read mask (and any documented bit filtering if specified), and compare against the documented default value; on mismatch, increment default-failure counter and log details. Masked write/read: For each test data pattern (e.g., all-ones, alternating bits, etc.), for each GPIO entry: if writable (write mask nonzero and not skipped), compute write_data = (pattern & write_mask) and write it to the register. Then, if readable (read mask nonzero and not skipped), read the register and compute read_data = (read_value & read_mask). Compute expected_data by combining bits: expected_writable = (pattern & read_mask & write_mask), expected_preserved = ((~write_mask) & read_mask & default_value); expected_data = (expected_writable | expected_preserved). Compare read_data vs expected_data; on mismatch, increment write/read-failure counter and log details. Completion: If both failure counters are zero, report PASS; otherwise report FAIL.

Feature: GPIO Negative-Edge Interrupt Enable and Validation
Test Description: Validate that each GPIO pad generates a negative-edge interrupt when configured. Configure per-pin control registers, enable group interrupt mask, generate a falling edge on each pad, confirm interrupt assertion and status, then clear and verify deassertion.
Meta Test Description: The test enables platform and system interrupt routing for GPIO, configures each per-pin GPIO control register starting from GP0_GPIO_8 with a 4-byte stride to set bits [20], [18], and [16], then iterates across 32 pads. For each pad index i: clear the raw interrupt status bit in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, enable the corresponding group interrupt mask bit in GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, and set a pending flag (int_pend=1). A stimulus register at 0xA0243ffc is first written with 0xffffffff, then toggled to ~wr_val where wr_val = (1<<i) to create a falling edge on the selected pad. The main loop waits (with timeout) for the default IRQ handler to run and clear int_pend. In Default_IRQHandler: set int_pend=0, drive 0xA0243ffc back to 0xffffffff, read the current pad’s per-pin control register (GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4) into rdata and verify (rdata & 0x1)==0 and (rdata & 0x2)!=0; read group status GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify the event bit (1<<i) is set; then reprogram the pad control register with bits [20] and [16] set, clear the raw status via GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, and confirm group status is 0. Finally, clear RAW_STCR1 for GPIO0/1 and clear the GIC IRQ (87/88). Any timeout or check failure increments test_err. finish(test_err) returns overall pass/fail.
Remarks: Ensure platform IRQs (87/88) are enabled and cleared during service; RAW_STCR1 must be written to de-assert system interrupt status after handling; per-pin control registers must be configured before enabling group interrupt masks; the external stimulus at 0xA0243ffc must be able to drive a falling edge on the targeted GPIO pad; verify group status is cleared after RAW status clear.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the platform interrupt for the GPIO instance(s) (IRQ 87/88) and enable the corresponding system interrupt in the interrupt enable register. 2) Initialize the external stimulus register to drive all pads high. 3) Configure each per-pin GPIO control register (starting at GP0_GPIO_8, word stride) to enable interrupt-related bits (including edge selection). 4) For each pad index i from 0 to 31: a) Clear the raw interrupt status for pad i in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1. b) Enable the group interrupt mask bit for pad i in the interrupt enable register. c) Generate a falling edge on pad i by first driving all pads high and then driving only pad i low via the stimulus register. d) Wait for the interrupt service routine to run (within timeout). 5) In the ISR (automatically invoked by the system): a) Restore the stimulus to drive pads high. b) Read the per-pin control register for the active pad and confirm input/edge bits reflect a valid negative-edge event. c) Read group interrupt status and confirm only the active pad bit is set. d) Clear the raw status for the active pad and confirm the group status clears to zero. e) Clear the system raw status and the corresponding GIC interrupt. 6) Declare PASS if all pads generate the expected negative-edge interrupts and all status clear operations succeed; otherwise FAIL.

Globals: unsigned int gpio_number, test_err, rdata, wr_val, i, addr1; extern int int_pend. Main test_case(): 1) test_err=0. 2) Conditionally enable GIC IRQs: if GPIO0 -> GIC_EnableIRQ(87); if GPIO1 -> GIC_EnableIRQ(88). 3) Conditionally enable system interrupt routing: if GPIO0 -> write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR); if GPIO1 -> write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR). 4) write_reg(0xA0243ffc, 0xffffffff). 5) for (i=0;i<32;i++): addr1 = MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4); write_reg(addr1, (1u<<20)|(1u<<18)|(1u<<16)); wait_on(10). 6) for (i=0;i<32;i++): wr_val = (1u<<i); write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, wr_val); write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, wr_val); wait_on(10); int_pend=1; write_reg(0xA0243ffc, 0xffffffff); wait_on(30); write_reg(0xA0243ffc, ~wr_val); unsigned int timeout=5000; while (int_pend && timeout--) { wait_on(10); } if (timeout==0) { printf("ERROR: Timeout waiting for GPIO%u negedge interrupt\n", (unsigned)(i+8)); test_err++; }. 7) finish(test_err). Default_IRQHandler(): 1) unsigned int rdata_grp, raddr, raddr2; unsigned int local_wr=(1u<<i); 2) int_pend=0; 3) write_reg(0xA0243ffc, 0xffffffff); 4) raddr = MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4); rdata = read_reg(raddr); 5) if ((rdata & 0x1)!=0) { test_err++; } 6) if ((rdata & 0x2)!=0x0) { rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1); if ((rdata_grp & local_wr)==0) { test_err++; } raddr2 = MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4); write_reg(raddr2, (1u<<20)|(1u<<16)); write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, local_wr); rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1); if (rdata_grp != 0x0) { test_err++; } ifdef GPIO0: write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR); GIC_ClearIRQ(87); ifdef GPIO1: write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR); GIC_ClearIRQ(88); } else { test_err++; }

Feature: GPIO Positive-Edge Interrupt Enable and Validation (All Pads)
Test Description: Validate that enabling positive-edge interrupts on all GPIO pads results in an interrupt for each pad upon a rising edge. Configure per-pin control registers for positive-edge detection, enable the group interrupt mask for all pads, generate rising edges, verify interrupt status, then clear and confirm deassertion.
Meta Test Description: The test configures platform and system interrupt routing for the GPIO block, programs all per-pin control registers (starting at the base per-pin register and continuing by word stride) for positive-edge interrupt detection, and enables the group interrupt mask for all pads. A stimulus source is toggled from low to high to create a positive (rising) edge on enabled pads. The main loop waits for the default interrupt handler to fire. In the ISR, the handler confirms the per-pin status/edge indicators, checks the group interrupt status bit(s) for the active pad(s), clears the raw status and verifies that the group status deasserts. The test iterates across all enabled pads (or handles all pad bits indicated by the group status) and records any timeout or mismatch as a failure before reporting the final result.
Remarks: Ensure platform interrupts for the GPIO instance are enabled and cleared during service. Configure positive-edge selection prior to enabling group masks. The external stimulus must be capable of generating rising edges on the targeted pads. Verify group status is cleared after raw status clear.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the platform and system interrupts for the GPIO instance. 2) Initialize the external stimulus to a known low level. 3) Configure all per‑pin GPIO control registers for positive‑edge interrupt detection. 4) Enable the group interrupt mask for all pads. 5) Generate a rising edge on the enabled pads using the external stimulus. 6) Observe that an interrupt is triggered and service it via the ISR. 7) In ISR processing, verify that the per‑pin and group interrupt status reflect the positive‑edge event. 8) Clear the raw interrupt status and confirm the group status deasserts. 9) Repeat/iterate to cover all pads that are enabled. 10) Declare PASS if all pads generate and clear interrupts as expected; otherwise FAIL.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure: Initialization: test_err=0. Enable platform IRQ(s) for the GPIO instance (e.g., GIC IRQ ID associated with GPIO0/1) and enable system interrupt routing in the SoC interrupt enable register. Configure all per-pin control registers (base_per_pin + i*4 for i over enabled pads) to select positive-edge interrupt mode; insert small waits if required. Enable the group interrupt mask register to allow all pad bits (e.g., write all-ones mask). Stimulus: drive external stimulus low, then transition to high to create positive edges (either one pad at a time using (1<<i) or all pads together via a full mask). Event handling: set a pending flag, then wait with timeout for ISR entry. In Default_IRQHandler: clear the pending flag; optionally restore stimulus to idle; read the active pad’s per-pin control/status register and check that input/edge status indicates a positive-edge event; read the group interrupt status register and confirm the corresponding bit(s) are set; write to the raw interrupt status clear register to clear the event bit(s); re-read the group status to confirm deassertion (zero). Also write the SoC raw status clear register and clear the GIC IRQ. Error accounting: any timeout waiting for ISR, missing status bit, or failure to clear increments test_err. Completion: finish(test_err).
Impacted Registers: GPIO GP0 per-pin control registers (GPIO_8 .. GPIO_39), GPIO GP0 Group Interrupt Enable 1, GPIO GP0 Group Interrupt Status 1, GPIO Raw Interrupt Status Clear 1, LSS SYSREG Interrupt Enable 1, LSS SYSREG Raw Status Clear 1
Meta Impacted Registers: MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 (+ i*4), MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if each enabled pad triggers a positive-edge interrupt upon a rising transition, the corresponding group status bit sets, and after clearing the raw status the group status reads zero. Any timeout or mismatch = FAIL.
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Timeout: if ISR not observed within the configured timeout after generating a rising edge, mark FAIL. Per‑pin check: per‑pin status indicates positive‑edge event when read post‑ISR. Group status set: group status register shows the bit(s) corresponding to the active pad(s).
